note: The eight family archives Record Atlas was generalised out of. This is not a directory of sources — it is what the method looks like when it is pointed at one family, and the reason the atlas exists at all. Descriptions are each archive's own.
lead: Record Atlas is the general tool. It was built out of eight one-family archives, each following a different line and all using the same method: every claim carries how sure it is and what it rests on.

archives.name: The Defranceschi Archive
archives.what: A family written down under eight sovereigns, in four languages, and spelled at least nine different ways.

archives.name: The Falco Archive
archives.what: Nine documented generations born, married and buried in one valley, and then a migrant ship to Brisbane.

archives.name: The Blažević Archive
archives.what: An evidence-first archive for the family of Hedviga Blažević of Senj — carriers, a tobacco factory, and a wall grave.

archives.name: The Lerena Archive
archives.what: A horse-dealer out of Argentina, a stable under Table Mountain, and four family traditions tested against the record rather than repeated.

archives.name: The D'Arcy Archive
archives.what: Out with the 39th Regiment in 1825, and four generations afterwards in two Brisbane cemeteries.

archives.name: The Mazza Archive
archives.what: Four Italian quarters — Mazza of Piedimonte Etneo, and Prostamo, Arena and Polistena of Calabria — ending in four graves in a row at Nudgee.

archives.name: The Booyzen Archive
archives.what: A Cape Dutch family that kept marrying British women, changed one letter of its name in a war, and came off the train at Johannesburg with nothing.

archives.name: The Luwinski Archive
archives.what: An evidence-first archive for the family of Lynn Derrick Luwinski — Berlin, Schubin, Sauerbaum, Lourenço Marques, Johannesburg, Porto.
